page: Amazon Web Services i3en.metal is a bare-metal storage-optimized server designed for high-throughput I/O and data-intensive computing. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, the bare-metal chassis provides 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs without hypervisor overhead. System memory comprises 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering 8.0 GB per vCPU. Attached storage consists of 60,000 GB (60 TB) of high-speed local NVMe SSDs, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded and memory-intensive capacity alongside average single-core speeds. The host achieved a strong stress-ng multi-core result of 81,867.78 and a PassMark CPU score of 57,184.5, contrasting with average single-core ratings in stress-ng (1,458.58) and Geekbench (1,327.0). Memory throughput is exceptionally high, recording 224.36 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 97.66 GB/sec in uncached writes. Furthermore, the platform demonstrated strong throughput in PassMark database operations (22,150.5), static web serving (50.77 GB/sec), and Redis SET execution at 77.09 million operations per second. Conversely, without hardware acceleration, LLM text generation remains weak to poor.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency and architectural tradeoffs, i3en.metal represents an extremely dense hardware deployment. The integration of 60 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage, 100 Gbps networking, and 768 GB of memory makes it cost-efficient for consolidating large-scale, I/O-heavy workloads that would otherwise require expansive distributed clusters. However, the reliance on previous-generation DDR4 memory and moderate per-core performance means it is less optimal for strictly compute-bound or single-threaded tasks.

Amazon Web Services i3en.metal is best suited for massive transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores such as Cassandra and MongoDB, data warehousing, search indexing, and real-time distributed file systems requiring high local disk space and extreme network transfer capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.metal is a storage-optimized bare-metal server featuring 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores) powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is configured with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory, 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and an expansive 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong multi-core processing, exceptional memory bandwidth (224.36 GB/sec large-block read), and superior data handling, highlighted by 77.09 million Redis SET operations per second and high PassMark database operational metrics. The architecture prioritizes massive local storage density and high network throughput, trading off absolute single-core execution speed and AI text generation efficiency. This bare-metal configuration is engineered for large transactional and NoSQL databases, data warehousing, distributed file systems, and high-throughput data processing workloads.
